source.repro: node --expose-gc plugins/comparative-adapters/benches/pafLineParse.bench.ts --rounds=25 for the minimap2 row, and the same with --only=big and PAF_BENCH_PATH set for the two PIF rows — the bench header carries the recipe that cuts those fixtures out of hs1ToMm39.over.chain.pif.gz. One process per fixture. Min of rounds, ranges over the runs whose control landed in 0.98-1.05; a run outside that measured nothing and is not quoted.
source.notes:
One line of text to one SyntenyFeature — the read path of both in-memory PAF adapters and both indexed PIF adapters. Two changes landed together and the bench reads them apart: `parsePAFLine` walking tab offsets instead of `line.split('\t')`, and the two feature builders dropping a `...rest` spread from the middle of their data-object literal.

The box was under load from other agents (load average ~7 of 16 cores), which is why the `both` column is a range rather than a figure; the ordering never moved across any run with a good control.

The feature build is the larger of the two changes on every fixture, which is the surprise — the cost model above, and ADR-039's note about it, are both written about the parse. Measured on their own, the parse is 1.49x (minimap2) to 1.84x (either PIF tier) and the data-object construction is 2.0-5.2x.

Row count is this harness's ceiling and it is low: past ~4,000 rows per arm the control falls to 0.63-0.79x while the candidate arms keep reporting plausible ratios. See BENCHMARKING.md; the bench warns above 6,000.
